newsitem.title: USA: Tax procrastinators get a chance to cry in their beer.
newsitem.headline: Tax procrastinators get a chance to cry in their beer.

text.p: A local restaurant is giving procrastinators a chance to have their tax forms professionally prepared as well as toast an expected refund -- or mourn what they owe Uncle Sam -- under one roof on April 15.

The owners of Dick's Last Resort, a local restaurant and bar, are teaming up with H&R Block Inc. to offer tax preparation services, food and libations to those who like to wait until April 15 to begin even thinking about income taxes.

The second annual Tax Deadline Day Celebration will offer special discount rates for tax return processing, and the person who winds up owing the most to the federal government will win a party at Dick's for up to 10 friends worth $500.
"We had several hundred people show up last year and we're expecting even more this year," a spokeswoman for the restaurant said.
She said about 100 people had their returns electronically filed by H&R Block at last year's event.
The festivities, which include an all-you-can-eat beef rib special for $10.40 and a special Tax Shelter Shooter cocktail, are scheduled to run for six hours.

Attendees are expected to bring their W-2s, 1099s and other pertinent documents along with the $32 fee for processing 1040A and 1040EZ forms. The price for a full 1040 filing is $64, and other charges apply for those who want a Refund Anticipation Loan from H&R Block.
State tax returns are included in the tax preparation fee and electronic filing is free, the restaurant said.
Food and drinks, of course, are extra and are not tax deductible.
